legacy_delta: community__design-principles.md and community__sdk-tiers.md are revision-agnostic community/process pages, not versioned spec pages; no legacy-delta content applies from them.

docs__2026-07-28__develop__clients__client-best-practices.md is specific to 2026-07-28 and references the caching utility spec page at /specification/2026-07-28/server/utilities/caching (new in this revision) and tools#output-schema / tools#error-handling / tools#security-considerations at /specification/2026-07-28/server/tools — these anchors did not exist under 2025-06-18/2025-11-25 wording in the same form since caching TTL/cacheScope hints and outputSchema are 2026-07-28 additions per this page's own references.

SDK tiering key dates place conformance tests as available 2026-01-23 and tiering published 2026-02-23 — this is a NEW governance mechanism relative to earlier revisions; no prior-revision tiering system is described in the source material read.

methods.name: tools/list
methods.params: (implied paginated list request; exact param/result field names not given in the four focus files — see schema.ts for authoritative shape, not read in this pass)
methods.result: List of tool definitions (name, description, inputSchema, optional outputSchema). Client Best Practices doc treats each tools/list result as carrying ttlMs and cacheScope hints per the caching utility (source: client-best-practices.md lines 145-149, citing /specification/2026-07-28/server/utilities/caching).
methods.notes: client-best-practices.md line 21: 'The host fetches tool definitions via tools/list as normal, but defers injecting them into the model's context' (progressive discovery pattern, a client-side recommendation, not a protocol requirement).

methods.name: notifications/tools/list_changed
methods.notes: client-best-practices.md line 140 and 148-149: hosts SHOULD 're-index the search catalog' on receipt, and MUST/SHOULD 'treat a cached list as stale once a list_changed notification arrives, even before its TTL expires' — this is a client-implementation recommendation tied to the caching utility, not stated as a protocol-level MUST in these pages.

methods.name: resources/read
methods.result: Per line 145-149, resources/read results also carry ttlMs and cacheScope caching hints per the caching utility spec page.
methods.notes: Referenced only for its caching-hint behavior; full param/result shape not in the four read files (would require reading schema.ts/resources spec pages, out of this pass's scope).

methods.name: server/discover
methods.params: none shown beyond illustrative sequence diagram
methods.notes: Shown in the Dynamic Server Management sequence diagram as the first call a host makes when connecting to a newly enabled server, before tools/list. This appears to be a 2026-07-28-era handshake method distinct from the older 'initialize' method; exact schema not given in focus files — flagged as an open question.

methods.name: tools/call
methods.params: Referenced generically as {name, args} for a stable meta-tool wrapper pattern (client-best-practices.md line 158-159) and as the dispatch target for sandbox-intercepted function calls (line 257: 'dispatches them as tools/call requests to MCP servers').
methods.result: On tool-level failure: 'a successful response with isError: true rather than a transport failure' (client-best-practices.md lines 296-298, citing /specification/2026-07-28/server/tools#error-handling).
methods.notes: Client Best Practices does not restate the full tools/call schema; it only documents the isError:true convention and that generated language-SDK wrappers SHOULD convert isError:true into a thrown/raised exception so model-authored code can use try/catch (line 298-299).

requirements.text: Implement a context-window-percentage threshold (recommended 1%-5%) for total tool-definition size; once tool definitions loaded upfront would exceed it, switch from loading-all-tools to progressive discovery.
For a small number of tools whose definitions occupy a small fraction of the context window, load all tool definitions directly instead of implementing progressive discovery.
When implementing progressive discovery via search, offer multiple response detail levels (name-only, name-and-description, full-schema) so the model can choose.
requirements.cite: client-best-practices.md line 138, Implementation Guidelines table row 'Offer multiple detail levels'

requirements.text: Cache/memoize tool definitions host-side once fetched from a server so re-injecting them later does not require another tools/list round trip; this cache is distinct from what is currently in the model's context.
Refresh (re-index) the search catalog when a server sends notifications/tools/list_changed.
Present/group tools organized by their source server so the model can reason about related capabilities.

Follow the ttlMs and cacheScope hints carried on each list result (e.g. tools/list), each server/discover result, and each resources/read result, per the specification's caching utility (/specification/2026-07-28/server/utilities/caching).
Treat a cached list as stale once a list_changed notification arrives, even before its TTL expires.

To preserve provider prompt-caching of the tools array: append newly discovered tool definitions after the cache breakpoint rather than re-sorting the tools array, OR route every call through a single stable call_tool({name,args}) meta-tool so the array never changes.
Treat server disconnection as a conversation-boundary operation rather than a per-turn operation, to avoid invalidating provider prompt caches unnecessarily.

When output schema is absent for a tool used in programmatic/code-mode calling, either (a) accept a generic type (any/string) and handle unstructured output downstream, or (b) use a host-brokered extract(value, ExpectedType) helper routed through the same stub-interception path (never a direct sandbox network call) to a fast auxiliary model, validating the result against ExpectedType before use.

In programmatic tool calling, apply the same human-in-the-loop confirmation / authorization policy to sandbox-originated tool calls as to direct calls; the host/broker remains the MCP host for spec purposes.

Grant categorical approval for a class of tool calls during a script run (e.g., 'allow ticketing_createIssue for this script run') instead of prompting per iteration, but the broker MUST still evaluate each call against that grant.

Apply the same input-review/untrusted-input policy to brokered (sandbox-to-server) tool results flowing to another server as to directly-model-mediated calls; output truncation alone is not sufficient to prevent exfiltration.
Give the sandbox direct network access; all external communication must flow through the host broker, which enforces authorization and access control.
Expose API keys/tokens/credentials to generated sandbox code; the host holds credentials and adds authentication when forwarding calls to servers.
Set timeouts and memory limits on sandbox execution to prevent runaway scripts.
Validate and truncate sandbox console output before feeding it back to the model.
Generated language-SDK wrappers around tools/call SHOULD convert an isError:true tool response into a thrown/raised exception so model-authored code can use try/catch.
If an uncaught error terminates a programmatically-generated script, surface the error as the script's result so the model can self-correct.
requirements.cite: client-best-practices.md lines 299-301 ('If an uncaught error terminates the script, surface it as the script's result')

requirements.text: MCP tool-level errors are represented as a successful protocol response carrying isError: true, not as a transport-level failure.
When a skill declares which MCP servers it needs (agent-skills integration), the host should connect those servers only when that skill is invoked, rather than eagerly at startup.
A Tier 1 SDK must implement all non-experimental protocol features and the optional capabilities sampling and elicitation ('complete protocol implementation').
A Tier 2 SDK is 'actively-maintained' and 'working toward full protocol specification support' (not yet complete).
Experimental features and protocol extensions (e.g., Tasks, MCP Apps) are not required for any tier (1, 2, or 3).
Tier 1: 100% conformance-test pass rate (of applicable required tests).
Tier 2: at least 80% conformance-test pass rate.
Tier 3: no minimum conformance pass rate.

Conformance scores are computed only over 'applicable required tests': tests for the spec version the SDK targets, excluding tests marked pending/skipped, excluding experimental-feature tests, excluding legacy backward-compat tests (unless the SDK claims legacy support), and excluding tests labeled 'disputed' until resolved.
Tier 1: support new protocol features before the next spec version release, on a timeline agreed per release based on feature complexity.
Tier 2: support new protocol features within 6 months of spec release.
Tier 1: triage new issues (label + validity determination, not resolution) within 2 business days.
Tier 2: triage issues within one month.
Tier 1: resolve critical (P0) bugs within 7 days.
Tier 2: resolve critical (P0) bugs within two weeks.
Tier 1 requires a stable release with clear versioning (idiomatic versioning, documented breaking-change policy).
Tier 2 requires at least one stable release.
A 'Stable Release' is a published version explicitly marked production-ready, e.g. 1.0.0 or higher, with no pre-release identifiers (-alpha, -beta, -rc).
Tier 1 documentation must be comprehensive with examples for all features.
Tier 2 documentation must at minimum cover core features (basic documentation).
Tier 1 and Tier 2 both require a published dependency update policy; not required for Tier 3.
Tier 1 requires a published roadmap that outlines concrete steps/work items tracking implementation of required (non-experimental, plus optional capabilities) MCP spec components.
Tier 2 requires a published plan toward Tier 1, or an explicit explanation for remaining at Tier 2.

SDK repositories must use consistent GitHub issue labels to enable automated triage-metric reporting: one Type label per issue (bug / enhancement / question, or native GitHub issue types as a substitute), one Status label (needs confirmation / needs repro / ready for work / good first issue / help wanted), and a Priority label when actionable (P0/P1/P2/P3), using these exact label names.

P0 (Critical) is defined as: security vulnerabilities with CVSS >= 7.0 (High/Critical), OR core-functionality failures that prevent basic MCP operations — connection establishment, message exchange, or use of core primitives (tools, resources, prompts).

An SDK may request tier advancement by self-assessing, opening a supporting-evidence issue in modelcontextprotocol/modelcontextprotocol, passing automated conformance testing, and receiving SDK Working Group maintainer approval (final assignment made by the Working Group).
Tier 1 -> Tier 2 relegation occurs if any conformance test on the latest stable release fails continuously for 4 weeks.
Tier 2 -> Tier 3 relegation occurs if more than 20% of conformance tests fail continuously for 4 weeks.
An SDK may also be relegated if issues remain unaddressed for two months (independent of the conformance-failure relegation trigger).

wire_details: _meta / caching keys: ttlMs and cacheScope are hint fields carried on tools/list, server/discover, and resources/read results per the caching utility (client-best-practices.md lines 145-147); exact field location (top-level vs _meta) and cacheScope enum values are NOT given in the four focus files — only named in prose, pointing to /specification/2026-07-28/server/utilities/caching, which was not part of this reading assignment (flag as open question / needs separate read of that spec page).
Notification method name: notifications/tools/list_changed (exact string, client-best-practices.md line 140, 148).

Error field: isError (boolean) on a tools/call result — 'a successful response with isError: true rather than a transport failure' (client-best-practices.md lines 296-298); no JSON-RPC error code is used for tool-execution failures, only this in-band boolean.
outputSchema is an optional field on a tool definition (client-best-practices.md line 178, 205), referenced via /specification/2026-07-28/server/tools#output-schema.

Method name referenced for server handshake in the dynamic-server-management diagram: server/discover (client-best-practices.md line 118) — returns 'Supported versions + capabilities' per the diagram; not otherwise documented in the four files.

Illustrative (non-normative, example-only) meta-tool/method names used for progressive discovery are host-invented, not protocol methods: search_tools, get_tool_details, search_available_servers, enable_server, disable_server, call_tool (client-best-practices.md lines 52-70, 112-127, 158-159) — these are host-side UX conventions, not part of the MCP wire protocol.
Stable-release version convention: 1.0.0 or higher, no pre-release identifiers -alpha, -beta, -rc (community__sdk-tiers.md line 53).
Tier-advancement issue tracker: modelcontextprotocol/modelcontextprotocol GitHub repo (community__sdk-tiers.md line 89).

Exact required GitHub label strings (must match verbatim): Type — bug, enhancement, question; Status — 'needs confirmation', 'needs repro', 'ready for work', 'good first issue', 'help wanted'; Priority — P0, P1, P2, P3 (community__sdk-tiers.md lines 113-141).
P0 CVSS threshold: >= 7.0 (High or Critical severity) (community__sdk-tiers.md line 145).
Key program dates: conformance tests available 2026-01-23; official SDK tiering published 2026-02-23 (community__sdk-tiers.md lines 12-19).
sdk_implications: The PowerShell SDK must implement, at minimum for Tier 2 candidacy: full protocol core (connection establishment/handshake, message exchange, tools, resources, prompts) since P0 bugs are defined around exactly these primitives — treat these as the non-negotiable conformance floor.

For Tier 1 candidacy the SDK must also implement sampling and elicitation as client-side optional capabilities, plus 100% of applicable (non-experimental, non-legacy-unless-claimed, non-pending, non-disputed) conformance tests for whichever spec version(s) it targets — plan explicit conformance-test-suite integration (from github.com/modelcontextprotocol/conformance) into CI from day one, since both tiers are graded mechanically against it.

Tasks and MCP Apps (protocol extensions) and other experimental features are explicitly optional at every tier — do not block a Tier 1/2 push on implementing them, but the roadmap should still state their status ('required roadmap' language covers only non-experimental + optional capabilities).

Client component MUST implement the isError:true convention for tool call failures — the PowerShell SDK's client-side tool-invocation wrapper should surface isError:true as a thrown PowerShell exception/terminating error (mirroring client-best-practices.md 'Generated wrappers should convert this into a thrown exception'), not as a normal return with a hidden error flag, to match idiomatic PowerShell error handling (try/catch, -ErrorAction) while staying protocol-correct.

If the SDK later supports building 'host' applications (agents) atop MCP clients, it should expose hooks for: tool-definition caching keyed off ttlMs/cacheScope, list_changed-triggered cache invalidation, and optional progressive-discovery helpers (a search/catalog layer) — these are best-practice/optional but a Tier-1-aspiring, feature-complete SDK would plausibly need extension points for host authors to implement them, even though the spec itself doesn't mandate a specific discovery API.

Repository hygiene for tier credibility: adopt GitHub's native issue types (bug/enhancement/question) or the exact label strings; set up Status and Priority labels verbatim as specified; document and observe issue-triage SLAs (2 business days for Tier 1 / 1 month for Tier 2) and P0 resolution SLAs (7 days / 2 weeks) from day one so historical metrics support a future tier-advancement request.

Ship a genuine 1.0.0 (no -alpha/-beta/-rc) as the 'Stable Release' gate for even Tier 2, with a documented semver/breaking-change policy ('clear versioning') and a published dependency-update policy — both required at Tier 1 and Tier 2.

Publish a roadmap document (even pre-1.0) enumerating required (non-experimental) spec components and their implementation status, since 'published roadmap' (Tier 1) / 'published plan toward Tier 1' (Tier 2) is a hard requirement, not just nice-to-have.

Because the repo is currently empty except MIT LICENSE and there is no local pwsh/dotnet SDK in this environment, actual implementation and conformance-test execution cannot happen in this sandbox — planning must assume CI (e.g. GitHub Actions with pwsh + .NET) will run the conformance suite; note this as an environment constraint for the plan.

Design-principles.md implies API design choices for the PowerShell SDK should favor a single idiomatic PowerShell pattern per concern (convergence over choice), build only the resources/tools/prompts primitives and let higher-level patterns (skills, apps, tasks) be layered by the host rather than baked into core cmdlets (composability over specificity), and support capability negotiation gracefully (interoperability over optimization) — i.e., the SDK's client must correctly perform capability negotiation and degrade when a server lacks sampling/elicitation/etc. rather than assuming full support.

'Stability over velocity' and 'pragmatism over purity' argue for a conservative, backward-compatible cmdlet/module API surface for the PowerShell SDK once 1.0 ships, since spec additions are permanent commitments SDKs must keep supporting.
open_questions: The four focus files do not give the full JSON-RPC shapes (params/result field names, required/optional) for tools/list, resources/read, or the newly-referenced server/discover method; these must be pulled from schema.ts / 2026-07-28_schema.json and the corresponding /specification/2026-07-28/server/* pages, which were out of scope for this pass.

The exact shape and enum values of the cacheScope hint and the ttlMs field's location (top-level field vs a _meta."io.modelcontextprotocol/..." key) are not stated in the read files — need the caching utility spec page (/specification/2026-07-28/server/utilities/caching) to get wire-level detail.

server/discover appears only in an illustrative mermaid sequence diagram in client-best-practices.md; it is unclear whether this is a real 2026-07-28 protocol method (replacing/complementing 'initialize') or purely illustrative host-invented terminology — must verify against schema.ts and the lifecycle/handshake spec page before treating it as normative.

community__sdk-tiers.md and community__design-principles.md are community-process pages without explicit revision binding (no '2026-07-28' path segment) — unclear whether tier requirements are versioned per spec revision or are a standing cross-revision governance policy; treat as currently-in-force policy but note it is not itself part of the versioned specification.

No PowerShell SDK is listed in the official SDK table (Tier 1: TypeScript, Python, C#, Go, Rust; Tier 2: Java, Ruby; Tier 3: Swift, PHP, Kotlin) — confirm whether an unlisted new-language SDK must first go through some onboarding/recognition process by the SDK Working Group before tiering applies at all, which is not addressed in these four pages.

Conformance test suite's actual applicable-test count/categories per spec version, and how percentage pass rate is computed with partial suites for a brand-new SDK, is not detailed here — need conformance_README.md / conformance_SDK_INTEGRATION.md (available locally per the task's file list but not read in this pass) to plan CI integration precisely.
source: docs/2026-07-28/develop/clients/client-best-practices.md; docs/2026-07-28/sdk.md; community/sdk-tiers.md; community/design-principles.md (all four read in full, no skimming)
summary: Client Best Practices (2026-07-28) is entirely client-side guidance (SHOULD/MAY, no protocol MUSTs) for scaling hosts across many tools/servers: progressive discovery (tools/list deferred injection, search_tools/get_tool_details meta-tools, context-window threshold 1-5%, caching via ttlMs/cacheScope per the caching utility, list_changed-triggered invalidation, prompt-cache-preserving append-only tool arrays) and programmatic tool calling / code mode (sandboxed script execution, host-brokered stub interception, no direct sandbox network access, no credential exposure, isError:true -> thrown exception convention, uncaught errors surfaced as script result). docs/sdk.md lists official SDKs and tiers: Tier 1 (TypeScript, Python, C#, Go, Rust), Tier 2 (Java, Ruby), Tier 3 (Swift, PHP, Kotlin) — no PowerShell SDK exists yet. community/sdk-tiers.md defines the tiering system precisely: conformance pass rate (100%/80%/none), feature-adoption timelines (per-release/6mo/none), issue triage SLA (2 business days/1 month/none), critical-bug SLA (7 days/2 weeks/none), stable-release and versioning requirements, documentation depth, dependency policy, roadmap; plus exact required GitHub label taxonomy, P0 definition (CVSS>=7.0 or core-primitive failure), advancement process, and relegation rules (any test failing 4 weeks: T1->T2; >20% failing 4 weeks: T2->T3; unaddressed issues 2 months). community/design-principles.md gives eight cross-cutting values (convergence, composability, interoperability, stability, capability-over-compensation, demonstration, pragmatism, standardization) guiding protocol evolution and, by extension, SDK API design conservatism.</summary>
